message:
feat(apk): the decoder inbox knows the reference chain; a recovery episode asks for an IDR at most 4 times; key requests carry their causes and are judged before they go (keepalive-r2 e, apk-decoder-inbox C r1, design r3)

Codex codex_apk_inbox_c_impl_go_r1.md (B1/B2 accepted as the pre-C baseline; C implementation and self-contrasts GO).
Branch feat/apk-inbox-c from 79b5c25; nothing on the wire, the limiter, the transport or a setting changes.

decoder_chain_inbox.hpp (pure logic, shared with the Windows tests):
- ChainInbox (8 frames / 4 MiB, as before): a duplicate / older AU (same generation, wrap-safe) dropped and counted;
  a frame over 4 MiB refused (a loss); a delta after a loss refused until an IDR after the loss point (the tail gap);
  on overflow the EARLIEST IDR whose IDR + suffix fits is kept and the older chain skipped (no loss), else the last
  IDR kept and the newest cut (a tail loss), else everything goes (a loss). A safety valve: 30 order drops in a row
  restart the order (counted). The assembler delivers in seq order (shared_core.cpp PopDelivery :906-915, :1058): the
  order checks are defensive.
- KeyRecoveryEpisode: one per loss; asks at t0 and 1 / 2 / 4 s after the previous SEND (at most 4); nothing while a
  usable IDR is preserved; a final 4 s window after the 4th, then exhausted (recorded once; a later usable IDR still
  decodes and ends it); closed only by an IDR after the loss point committed to the codec; a candidate lost again
  resumes the same episode; invalidated by a pick / bind / unbind / stream reset / abort / surface.
decoder_key_request.hpp: DecoderKeyRequest -- a cause set (recovery / codec-up / abort / owed / pipeline / legacy) +
the sink epoch, the episode, the owed token; Merge keeps every cause.

android_video_decoder.cpp/.hpp: the chain inbox at the RX door; await-key and the pending slot's drops are chain
losses of the same episode (the slot's loss point is the dropped frame, not the arriving IDR); the episode closes at
CommitQueue; a candidate is an IDR after the loss point in the inbox, the pending slot or going in; while the
selection is owed an IDR (gate KeyLost / Rearm, the session's 8 x 1 s asks) the episode adds no ask of its own (one
logical exchange, not 4 + 8). New hooks TakeDecoderKeyRequest / DecoderKeyRequestValidCauses /
OnDecoderKeyRequestSent (and *As, entry_sink_adapter.hpp for the binding). DebugStatus: chainSkipped chainDup
chainStale tailGap recovery episode asks episodes recClosed recExhausted recWants recSent recMoot keyTaken keyEpoch.
Unchanged: N1 reservation / KeyDelivered, 21 creates, the 2 s detach, RX / control never wait for the codec.

native_video_client_session.cpp/.hpp (shared API: defaulted virtuals; a sink without them behaves as before): the
want is taken with its descriptor and kept HELD (limiter refused) or ACCEPTED (pending); the held one is judged by
the sink before the limiter again, the accepted one right before the KeyframeRequest exchange -- none valid: not
sent (KeyRequestsDroppedStale). The sink is told when the exchange started (its retry clock). The sink's own wants
are also taken on every control pass (a retry falls due on the clock). The ledger clears with the old resets.

Tests (Windows, the product sink against the stand-in NDK):
- decoder_chain_inbox_test 45/45 (the decision table, the episode, the descriptor).
- android_decoder_inbox_test 12/12 (the r1 baseline [1]-[6], all FAIL at ac587dd except [6]): [2]'s last 10 deltas
  are now paced 3 ms like the rest of the case -- sent at once they are a second loss of their own (10 > 8),
  checked as such in the new [2b]; the Rx stand-in takes the descriptor and reports the send, as the session does.
- android_decoder_inbox_c_test 31/31 (new, plain build): order / wrap, an IDR over 4 MiB, a candidate lost again,
  t0/1/3/7 + exhausted (~11 s) + a later IDR still decodes, D8 validity (pick, commit, merged causes, abort, late
  send), the binding adapter (owner / park / unbind), a 4 s overload (bounded; restarts at the NEWEST IDR), a 3 s
  held create.
- fixture alignment: owed_key / binding / decode_stats / liveness built frames with seq 0 (every frame the same AU to
  an order-aware inbox) -- now an increasing seq as the assembler delivers.
- criteria changed by the policy (design r3 replaces r1's drop-the-oldest): liveness [6] -- the IDR is now KEPT
  (nothing owed) and the tail loss is one episode with one ask; [12] -- the refused IDR is owed and asked through that
  duty, the sink adds no second ask.
- regressions: owed_key 32/32, geometry 10/10, binding 17/17, decode_stats 42/42, liveness 68/68, session_liveness
  9/9, pending_slot 21/21, client_session_prelogin_select 60/60; the whole tree builds (0 errors).
Not yet: the session-level D8 contrast, mutants and the 79b5c25 negative runs, NDK 4 ABI. No device run.
